examples.scenario: Dynamic CRS is used without coordinate epoch.
examples.reason: Dynamic coordinates require explicit epoch provenance.

examples.scenario: Coordinate epoch is replaced by transformation central epoch.
examples.reason: Observation epoch and model central epoch are distinct.

examples.scenario: Time-dependent Helmert executes with missing time by central-epoch fallback.
examples.reason: Successful execution does not prove correct epoch.

examples.scenario: Source epoch is supplied but target epoch is omitted for dynamic target CRS.
examples.reason: Target dynamic coordinate state is incomplete.

examples.scenario: Target epoch is supplied but source epoch is omitted for dynamic source CRS.
examples.reason: Source dynamic coordinate state is incomplete.

examples.scenario: Epoch 2026 is treated as a calendar label rather than decimal year.
examples.reason: PROJ epoch parameters use decimal years.

examples.scenario: GPS week is passed directly to a Helmert step expecting decimal years.
examples.reason: Temporal unit conversion is required.

examples.scenario: Temporal unit conversion is performed but omitted from pipeline provenance.
examples.reason: T-axis semantics must be replayable.

examples.scenario: Fourth coordinate column is interpreted as Z rather than T.
examples.reason: x,y,z,t order must be fixed.

examples.scenario: cct -t overrides per-point observation times without manifest entry.
examples.reason: A global time override changes all points.

examples.scenario: cct -z is confused with coordinate epoch.
examples.reason: Height and time are separate dimensions.

examples.scenario: HUGE_VAL time is accepted as a valid epoch.
examples.reason: HUGE_VAL denotes absent time in documented API usage.

examples.scenario: PROJ 9.3 and 9.4 epoch behavior is treated as identical.
examples.reason: CRS@epoch syntax and epoch framework changed.

examples.scenario: Source --s_epoch differs between primary and replay.
examples.reason: Dynamic source state changed.

examples.scenario: Target --t_epoch differs between primary and replay.
examples.reason: Dynamic target state changed.

examples.scenario: Deformation t_epoch and dt are both supplied.
examples.reason: They are mutually exclusive.

examples.scenario: Deformation dt is inferred from file date.
examples.reason: Time interval must come from declared transformation semantics.

examples.scenario: A Helmert rate parameter changes but static parameters match.
examples.reason: Kinematic result changes with rate.

examples.scenario: Observation-minus-central epoch interval changes by 0.1 year.
examples.reason: Rate propagation changes.

examples.scenario: Time-dependent operation is accepted without checking requires-per-coordinate-time API.
examples.reason: Operation time requirement must be explicit.

examples.scenario: Operation candidate set changes when epoch metadata changes.
examples.reason: Operation selection provenance changed.

examples.scenario: Pipeline text matches but source epoch differs.
examples.reason: Epoch metadata is part of execution state.

examples.scenario: Epoch manifest matches but pipeline digest differs.
examples.reason: Coordinate operation semantics changed.

examples.scenario: Survey acquisition year is copied into coordinate epoch.
examples.reason: Survey date and reference-frame epoch are different concepts.

examples.scenario: Dataset revision date is used as coordinate epoch.
examples.reason: Publication metadata is not coordinate time.

examples.scenario: Current year is used because coordinate epoch is unknown.
examples.reason: Unknown epoch must fail closed.

examples.scenario: Midpoint of survey interval is used as coordinate epoch.
examples.reason: No authoritative coordinate epoch evidence exists.

examples.scenario: ETRS89 is treated as timeless because its name contains 1989.
examples.reason: Reference-system name is not per-coordinate epoch.

examples.scenario: ETRS89 and WGS84 are treated as identical at high precision.
examples.reason: OS distinguishes its ETRS89 realization for precise GB positioning.

examples.scenario: EPSG:4937 is replaced with a 2D ETRS89 CRS while Z is retained.
examples.reason: Ellipsoidal-height semantics changed.

examples.scenario: EPSG:9452 compound height CRS loses its vertical component.
examples.reason: Mean-sea-level height provenance is removed.

examples.scenario: OSTN15 operation ID is not recorded.
examples.reason: Horizontal transform identity must be pinned.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 operation ID is not recorded.
examples.reason: Vertical transform identity must be pinned.

examples.scenario: OSTN15 is used to infer ODN height without OSGM15.
examples.reason: Horizontal and vertical transformations are separate.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 is used without ETRS89 ellipsoidal-height input provenance.
examples.reason: Vertical conversion input semantics are incomplete.

examples.scenario: OS Net ETRS89 realization is replaced by generic WGS84 coordinates.
examples.reason: High-precision GB frame provenance changed.

examples.scenario: Archived ETRS89 source coordinates are discarded after conversion.
examples.reason: OS recommends retaining ETRS89 archive coordinates.

examples.scenario: OSTN02 output is directly compared with OSTN15 output as same realization.
examples.reason: OS advises returning to ETRS89 before forward conversion.

examples.scenario: A slight ETRS89 realization change is ignored during legacy reconciliation.
examples.reason: OSTN15 update includes realization changes.

examples.scenario: Coordinate epoch is rounded to integer year before transform.
examples.reason: Decimal-year precision can affect kinematic result.

examples.scenario: Coordinate epoch is rounded after transform and reused as input.
examples.reason: Replay must preserve original epoch precision.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent epoch manifests differ by 0.001 year.
examples.reason: Epoch identity did not reproduce.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent T-axis values differ although output XYZ matches.
examples.reason: Equal spatial output does not prove equal temporal provenance.

examples.scenario: Primary 4D pipeline drops T after first step.
examples.reason: Time-dependent downstream steps need temporal state.

examples.scenario: Independent replay inserts T only at Helmert step.
examples.reason: 4D coordinate history differs.

examples.scenario: Output epoch is omitted from transformed-point record.
examples.reason: Dynamic target state must be auditable.

examples.scenario: Output epoch is copied from input without operation evidence.
examples.reason: Target epoch semantics must follow the operation.

examples.scenario: Static CRS is assigned a coordinate epoch and treated as dynamic.
examples.reason: Epoch options apply to dynamic CRS semantics.

examples.scenario: Dynamic CRS is downgraded to static to avoid missing epoch.
examples.reason: Missing provenance cannot be bypassed.

examples.scenario: A time-dependent operation is replaced by a static transform because T is unavailable.
examples.reason: Do not silently remove temporal behavior.

examples.scenario: A ballpark transform is used when epoch-aware operation fails.
examples.reason: Approximate fallback is not terminal evidence.

examples.scenario: An explicit operation is replaced by implicit CRS-to-CRS selection.
examples.reason: Candidate selection may change.

examples.scenario: Operation name matches but operation identifier differs.
examples.reason: Names are insufficient for exact operation identity.

examples.scenario: Coordinate epoch is stored as locale-formatted date text.
examples.reason: Decimal-year numeric representation must be stable.

examples.scenario: Decimal comma is used for epoch in one replay.
examples.reason: Canonical numeric parsing must not depend on locale.

examples.scenario: Leap-year handling changes decimal-year conversion implementation.
examples.reason: Date-to-decimal-year mapping must be reproducible.

examples.scenario: Survey timestamp timezone is used to derive coordinate epoch without geodetic metadata.
examples.reason: Observation date alone is insufficient.

examples.scenario: ETRS89 original 1989 context is reported as every coordinate's epoch.
examples.reason: System realization context is not per-coordinate time.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 height is emitted with no ODN label.
examples.reason: Output height datum must remain explicit.

examples.scenario: ODN height is treated as ellipsoidal height after reverse transform.
examples.reason: Vertical semantics changed.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but an epoch-aware transform is run on guessed coordinates.
examples.reason: Canonical point must bind the operation.

examples.scenario: Canonical point exists but its CRS/epoch provenance is absent.
examples.reason: Coordinates alone are insufficient.

examples.scenario: Exact boundary is absent but epoch-aware output is labelled parcel-final.
examples.reason: Parcel context remains unbound.

examples.scenario: Static epoch tests pass and numeric elevation is emitted.
examples.reason: Target runtime has not executed.

examples.scenario: Fixture 4D coordinate is copied into target output.
examples.reason: Examples are validation only.

examples.scenario: Epoch-runtime rows are marked complete without runner output.
examples.reason: Fresh execution evidence is absent.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known host issue remains BLOCKED.

examples.scenario: A second runner is launched for epoch probing.
examples.reason: Continuation permits only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 source readiness is reported as epoch-transform accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation confidence is not measured target accuracy.

examples.scenario: Output XYZ matches to display precision but epoch differs.
examples.reason: Temporal provenance remains part of the coordinate.

examples.scenario: Input T-axis is silently dropped by a serializer.
examples.reason: 4D tuple must remain 4D.

examples.scenario: Operation central epoch is changed while rates remain fixed.
examples.reason: Rate propagation interval changes.

examples.scenario: Coordinate epoch is changed while central epoch remains fixed.
examples.reason: Kinematic output changes.

examples.scenario: Primary uses CRS@epoch while replay uses T-axis only with no equivalence proof.
examples.reason: Different epoch mechanisms must be shown equivalent.

examples.scenario: Batch 95 is reported as final parcel height difference.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary and runtime numeric sampling remain absent.

examples.scenario: Numeric height difference is emitted without transformed-point epoch provenance.
examples.reason: Temporal coordinate state is still unverified.
